question: What is the dimensionality d_model and number of attention heads in the base Transformer model?
expected_answer: In the base Transformer model, d_model = 512 and the number of attention heads h = 8 (with dk = dv = 64).
expected_citations: [Attention Is All You Need, Sec 3.2.2 Multi-Head Attention, p. 5]

question: What is the sampling frequency and frame rate of the Mimi neural audio codec?
expected_answer: Mimi operates at an input/output audio sampling rate of 24 kHz and produces a frame rate of 12.5 Hz (downsampling by a factor of 1920).
expected_citations: [Moshi: a speech-text foundation model for real-time dialogue, Sec 3.3 Audio Tokenization, p. 8]

question: What is the objective of the ratio loss in Dynamic Chunking?
expected_answer: The ratio loss guides the boundary predictor (routing module) to adhere to a targeted compression ratio (average chunk size) without explicit tokenization supervision.
expected_citations: [Dynamic Chunking for End-to-End Hierarchical Sequence Modeling, Sec 2.2.3 Ratio Loss, p. 8]

question: How does H-Net's sequence processing complexity compare to standard Transformer self-attention complexity with respect to input sequence length n?
expected_answer: Standard Transformer self-attention per layer has O(n^2 * d) complexity with O(1) sequential operations. H-Net reduces byte-level sequence length by chunking into hierarchical levels, reducing the quadratic attention overhead over the original byte sequence length.
expected_citations: [Attention Is All You Need, Sec 4 Why Self-Attention, p. 6]
[Dynamic Chunking for End-to-End Hierarchical Sequence Modeling, Sec 2 H-Net Architecture, p. 4]

question: Both Moshi and Dynamic Chunking address sequence representation without standard words. How do their token granularities compare (audio frames vs raw bytes)?
expected_answer: Moshi compresses continuous 24 kHz audio waveforms into discrete acoustic/semantic tokens at 12.5 Hz using the Mimi RVQ codec. Dynamic Chunking eliminates word/BPE tokenizers by processing text directly at the byte level with dynamic learned chunk boundaries.
expected_citations: [Moshi: a speech-text foundation model for real-time dialogue, Sec 3.3 Audio Tokenization, p. 9]
[Dynamic Chunking for End-to-End Hierarchical Sequence Modeling, Sec 1 Introduction, p. 1]

question: What BLEU score was achieved by the Transformer (big) model on the WMT 2014 English-to-German translation test in Table 2?
expected_answer: The Transformer (big) model achieved a BLEU score of 28.4 on the WMT 2014 English-to-German translation test.
expected_citations: [Attention Is All You Need, Sec 6.1 Machine Translation, p. 8]

question: In Table 4 of the Moshi paper, how does Mimi compare to the RVQGAN baseline on subjective MUSHRA quality?
expected_answer: Mimi achieved a MUSHRA score of 78.4 (at 1.1 kbps) or higher across configurations, outperforming RVQGAN which scored significantly lower under comparable bitrates.
expected_citations: [Moshi: a speech-text foundation model for real-time dialogue, Sec 5.2 Audio Tokenization, p. 23]

question: In Table 1 of the Dynamic Chunking paper, how does the byte-level H-Net compare to compute-matched token-based Transformers?
expected_answer: The byte-level H-Net matches or slightly outperforms compute- and data-matched token-based Transformers in bits-per-character (BPC) and downstream accuracy without using a BPE tokenizer.
expected_citations: [Dynamic Chunking for End-to-End Hierarchical Sequence Modeling, Sec 3.1 Language Modeling, p. 11]

question: In Scaled Dot-Product Attention, what is the exact mathematical scaling factor applied to the query-key dot products before the softmax?
expected_answer: The scaling factor is 1 / sqrt(d_k), dividing the dot products by the square root of the key dimension d_k.
expected_citations: [Attention Is All You Need, Sec 3.2.1 Scaled Dot-Product Attention, p. 4]

question: What is the function of the 'Inner Monologue' in Moshi, and why is it delayed relative to the user audio?
expected_answer: The Inner Monologue models text tokens as an intermediate step before generating speech tokens, predicting text slightly ahead of speech synthesis to align semantic and acoustic reasoning.
expected_citations: [Moshi: a speech-text foundation model for real-time dialogue, Sec 3.4.4 Inner Monologue, p. 15]

question: How does Dynamic Chunking backpropagate gradients through discrete boundary decisions without explicit boundary labels?
expected_answer: Dynamic Chunking uses a Straight-Through Estimator (STE) and a smoothing module to allow continuous gradient flow during training while making hard discrete chunking decisions.
expected_citations: [Dynamic Chunking for End-to-End Hierarchical Sequence Modeling, Sec 2.2 Dynamic Chunking (DC), p. 6]
